svg.title: Proposed folder structure of Tell and Wire, second version
svg.desc: The main architecture drawing with one folder per box, checked in a trial run; folders and files a cleanup would move are marked in orange.
svg.text: Proposed folder structure, second version: each box one folder, what would move in orange

The moves of A to D were tried on a throwaway branch: 98 files touched, typecheck, lint and every test green but the one that wants the documents to name the new folders. The rename of serve's option and the test of E were not. An orange frame is a
folder that does not exist yet; "was ..." says where a file is now. Nothing is moved.
▶ Run: the tool as it runs, in the editor
asking ✨ for a graph, and its rule
what changed in the project on disk
a dialog asked from code, answered as a promise
a folder listing, set and shown
what a value looks like on a card
the graph as the editor sees it
a graph as the editor holds it
the open graph and its views
stays: it sits below the writing pieces
wires the pieces of writing/: stays, writing/ may not
one ✨ in flight; what the chats ask
how a person edits each kind
the host's routes and its own, by name
Tell & Wire offered to an assistant
a node's files, a whole graph
the prose a writer is told
the dialog and the one file behind it
a round kept as a test
the prompts a node is written with
the page, windows standing in it
Ask, Do, Show; the window as a graph
under the page: cells, hood, debug
the open notebook; windows as a graph to
its look, and the tool's scheme on the
a tool as fixed windows; read back
a product has one folder named for it in each tier: graph/ gui/ backend/ frontend/ -- and the two know each other only by /api/product, /api/switch and ?open=
the graph; does the wiring hold
how a graph runs: stays, 60 importers
the colour scheme, for every GUI
the room what a node hands on is shown in
Authoring: a folder named so is not carried
a model's transcript; a project written
switching products: stays, only such a folder stays out of a package
run, or serve; the Product plug
the editor and the notebook run on it
its end of the GUI port
the graph in use; one round at a time
a tool that starts by itself: the host's, only session.ts uses it
stays: the GUI side of the backend, graph and GUI apart all the way
the engine behind the core protocol
a code body in a sandbox
tools for a model, from MCP servers
What I take back, and what stays (and why)
Dropped from the first version: backend/switch/
Only a folder named editor, notebook or authoring stays out of a package. Product switching starts programs; in backend/switch/ every package would
carry it. It stays in authoring.
Dropped: views/ into node/, the ✨ logic into writing/
The editor's layers are ranks: views (3, pure drawing) and writing (5) lie below node (6), which wires them. Moved the other way, a lower folder would
One file, on purpose: the GUI side of the backend, as frontend/deployment/gui is its side of the browser. Graph and GUI are apart all the way.
Dropped: splitting host/, runtime/, graph/ by role
Twelve files with distinct names each are not scattered, only long. Dozens of importers would change for no gain in where things are.
Kept on purpose: the four faces of a kind
Definition, authoring design, runner or view, builder: each in the tier that needs it, named alike (a test holds it). A kind-first folder would mix what
a package carries with what it does not.
A. The notebook's frontend in one folder
frontend/notebook/{gui,graph,document,elements}, as the editor has gui and graph. Its layers test keeps the two as siblings; the strip rule loses two
B. In the editor, a folder is a rank
document/ now holds ranks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7. elements/, fields/ (two folders into one) and dialogs/ stand beside it; four loose files go to app/ with the
The architecture says the clock is the host's; only session.ts uses it, and it stands in the engine's folder.
D. Names that say one thing each
gui/windows.ts beside gui/windows/ becomes room.ts; scheme.ts is every GUI's and leaves windows/; ai/mcp.ts becomes tools.ts and the MCP server for
assistants gets assistant/ (four things were called mcp); the option "editor" of serve becomes "product", the notebook uses it too.
E. The sharing rule, held by a test
Common code names no product in its code, only in comments: after D that holds everywhere but the start-up (cli.ts), where the products are plugged in.
The first "if notebook" in a shared file is then the test failing: give each product its own.
